favorites.name: bobblune
favorites.reason: Bobble plus a shortened lune is a little moon bobbing, and the repeated b makes it friendly, shoutable, and easy to recall after one noisy hearing. It stays on the playful surface, so the hidden ocean and the lens remain for other names.

favorites.name: enceluddle
favorites.reason: Encel- with a puddle and cuddle ending makes the ocean moon intimate enough to splash in and gather around. A listener may hear the cuddle before the astronomy, and that warmth is worth one spoken correction.

favorites.name: zorbelune
favorites.reason: Zorb and lune name the central change, a playful sphere taking on a moon, and both halves are clear on a first pass. Ice, plume, and projection stay implied, which is why the glowing and plume names stay beside it.

favorites.name: fathomoon
favorites.reason: Depth and the act of understanding share one m with moon, so looking into the ocean inside the moon is audible. The tone is grave beside the froth, and the double reading is still the clearest whole-project metaphor.

favorites.name: cryzorcean
favorites.reason: Ice, the sphere, and the ocean collide in one compact center, which is the transformation in miniature. The stress is ambiguous and the spelling needs a moment of teaching, and the three-part picture is worth that hearing.

favorites.name: waxfathom
favorites.reason: Wax and fathom stay whole, so a brightening moon, a water depth, and the act of understanding can be retold without a glossary. It sits far down the averaged list because it is solemn and barely a coinage, and the honest triple is why it stays.

favorites.name: rimeverie
favorites.reason: Frost and reverie, joined on the shared e and the repeated r, make a cold daydream that is pronounceable on the first try. It is thin on delight and on the sphere, so it carries the astral mood of the piece.

favorites.name: splunelle
favorites.reason: Splash opens it and luna sits in the middle, so it sounds like a small luminous moon someone could call across a field. Aurora leaves no fragment, and the sound still earns the slot with one sentence of help for the color.

favorites.name: zorbilume
favorites.reason: The sphere and an inner glow meet in one short, clear word, the projection half of the same object zorbelune makes lunar. Lume reads as light, so Enceladus stays outside this one.

favorites.name: frothalo
favorites.reason: A halo of bubbles is round, bright, and usefully a little ridiculous, which a burn can shout. The dropped h makes halo a near-reading, and the moon stays implied.

favorites.name: causticuddle
favorites.reason: The shared c turns a bright concentrated water-light pattern into bodily closeness, a satisfying oxymoron and easy to remember. Caustic needs its optical meaning said aloud once, and Saturn stays outside the name.

favorites.name: selenerime
favorites.reason: Selene and rime are both audible, giving a quiet mythic ice-moon title just outside the averaged cut. Rime is easy to hear as rhyme, and play and the crowd stay outside the name.

favorites.name: geysergleam
favorites.reason: Geyser and gleam state a plume becoming projected light with both words intact, the plain Enceladus signature the denser meshes lose. It is a compound, and that plainness is why it remains.

favorites.name: breathalo
favorites.reason: Breath and halo fuse into a living ring of light, a credible story of presence and a body briefly cast outward. It never touches the moon or the water, so it returns beside the lunar names as the human one.

favorites.name: aquiferime
favorites.reason: Aquifer and rime stay fully readable, so water held under frost is an honest picture of the buried ocean, with a side-hearing of rhyme. It is cooler than a festival shout and well below the averaged cut, and the subject's accuracy is why it outruns prettier names that miss the hidden water.

weight_rationale: A Love Burn name has to survive a noisy first hearing and be retold that night, so sayability, memory, character, holistic fit, and the story people repeat outweigh clever machinery. The moon is a real subject and gets 7, but watery light, a body, and shared delight can carry a name that never says Saturn. Preference and grok_preference together are 16, enough to swing a near tie toward a name worth shouting, and not enough to rescue a consonant pile. Roots stay at 5 so pretended etymology is punished while perfectly recoverable keyword stacks still lose on character, wordplay, and inventiveness. Inventiveness is 4 because illegible novelty is the common failure in this set; when a coinage is both fresh and coherent, character and wordplay already record the win.
